problem:
In **ascending order**, the vertical asymptotes of $f(x)=\frac{x+2}{{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4x+4}$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}} $\,$ and $\,x=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+2}{{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4x+4} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{{x}^{2}(x-1)-4(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{({x}^{2}-4)(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{x+2}{(x-2)(x+2)(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x+2}}{(x-2)\cancel{(x+2)}(x-1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(x-2)(x-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
(x-2)(x-1)=0
$$

This gives the solutions $x=1$ and $x=2.$ 

Therefore, in ascending order, the equations of the vertical asymptotes are $x=1$ and $x=2.$
